answer: Each agent must bond scarce computation to a public key, then earn standing through tasks whose outputs are checked by independently sampled peers; one key cannot multiply that bond or its accumulated reputation. A newcomer can still join, but to flood the network with fake identities an attacker must lock up more compute per identity and risk losing it when peers catch forged work. Even across a tundra-wide network, the river of rewards follows verified contribution, not the number of names an attacker can forge.
